chapter: Leaving Hampton and starting his own band
title: Convalescing at home with Dr. Mayer's exercises
summary: Dr. Mayer visited Cobb's Long Island house and gave him seven weeks of exercises so he could walk on a walker and crutches.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So (inaudible) IN A WAY You come out of the first operation. You get ready to start (WORKING), but then you have to go in for the second, which we talked about yesterday. So now when you've got (inaudible) through the second, now what happens?
I recover from (inaudible) on the second operation?
Well, after you've had this long
period in bed after the second operation --

-- I come out for convalescing. My doctor came to my house -- something unusual -- I'm living in Long Island, Jamaica, that is, Brick Town, and Dr. Mayer came out to my house and gave me exercises for seven weeks to get me prepared to get up out of bed. He tested my spine with his thumb going down to see if I felt any pain, and I don't feel it.

So he gave me to lay on my stomach, to flex my back and raise up (inaudible) as hard as I could every hour on the hour. He gave me muscle situations for my legs, and I did this religiously. When I got up, I had one day on the walker, one day. And second day they put me on the crutches, and that's how he got me prepared. Seven weeks -- I didn't even know I'd been in bed.
But without the exercises to build my muscles up before I come to the hospital --
